newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila wheat buyers say to stay out of market.
newsitem.headline: Manila wheat buyers say to stay out of market.

text.p: Most Philippine flour millers are expected to stay out of the market in the next few weeks awaiting a projected decline in wheat prices, traders said on Friday.

"There are no new developments as millers are waiting for market prices to slide. With bumper harvest around the world, prices are expected to slide to $4 a bushel in the coming weeks," a trader said.
"The existing price of wheat is not reflective of the market situation. There is more than enough supply so we expect prices to go down," the trader added.
Aside from waiting for prices to soften, traders said most of the local millers are also fully stocked up to the Christmas season.

This week only one transaction was recorded when a local flour mill bought on Tuesday 25,000 tonnes of U.S. dark northern spring wheat at $4.10 a bushel and 10,000 tonnes of western white wheat at $4.18 a bushel.

The Department of Trade and Industry said prevailing retail price of hard flour in Metro Manila dropped to 290 pesos ($11.15) from 300 pesos ($11.54) while price of soft flour softened to 260 pesos ($10) from 285 pesos ($10.96).

The state-run National Food Authority said that while the average retail price of white corn dropped to 10.67 pesos (41.03 cents) per kilogram from 11.22 pesos (43.15 cents), yellow corn increased to 10.30 pesos (39.61 cents) from 10.27 pesos ($39.5 cents) per kg.
